sections.title: Arduino fundamentals
sections.summary: Inputs, outputs, pins, sketches and serial monitoring.
sections.content:
Level 1: Electronics & Arduino Foundations

Learn the fundamentals of electricity, including voltage, current, resistance, power, and Ohm’s Law.
Understand how Arduino boards work and how they connect programming with real-world electronics.
Explore basic components and circuits while building the foundation needed for more advanced engineering projects.
See how Arduino technology is used in applications ranging from sensors and motors to prosthetics and scientific experiments.
Biomedical Engineering Track

Apply electronics and programming to the human body and biomedical systems.
Work with sensors such as heart-rate, temperature, and EMG muscle sensors.
Learn how to analyze noisy, variable real-world biological signals and turn data into meaningful feedback.
Complete increasingly independent projects, including human-monitoring systems and other biomedical engineering applications.

Electrical Engineering Track
Build larger, more advanced electronic systems that function like real products and mechanisms.
Work with components such as transistors, DC motors, displays, capacitors, and external power supplies.
Combine sensing, actuation, and feedback to create interactive hardware projects.
Emphasize experimentation, problem-solving, iteration, and self-directed engineering design.

sections.title: Circuits and components
sections.summary: LEDs, resistors, breadboards, buttons and safe prototyping.
sections.content: Build simple circuits safely and understand how common electronic components work together. This section can include breadboard layout, LEDs, resistors, buttons, basic circuit diagrams, power and ground connections, and safe prototyping habits.

sections.title: Sensors and data
sections.summary: Read physical inputs, interpret measurements and trigger responses.
sections.content: Connect sensors to Arduino projects and turn physical measurements into useful data. This section can cover reading sensor values, calibrating measurements, viewing data through the Serial Monitor, setting thresholds, and making a project respond to changing inputs.

sections.title: Motors and control
sections.summary: Use servos and motors to make projects move and react.
sections.content: Add movement to projects using servos and other motors. This section can cover controlling position and speed, supplying motors safely, using external control components when needed, and combining sensors with movement to create responsive systems.

sections.title: Project engineering
sections.summary: Define a problem, prototype, test, debug, document and present.
sections.content: Bring coding and engineering skills together in a complete project. This section can guide members through defining a problem, planning a solution, building a prototype, testing and debugging, documenting their work, improving the design, and presenting the final result.
